objective_of_smoke: Prove the HiGS sparse-tile kernel executes natively (not dense-render-then-mask) and that changing tile_mask produces the expected change in selected tile / intersection / blend workload, with correct gradients.

gate_B.description: rasterize_gaussian_higs_dynamic exists and supports explicit tile mask
gate_B.sampled_ratio_semantics: fraction of tiles selected by mask; tile_sampling_ratio=1.0 is dense

gate_C.description: loaded Python module / main CUDA ext / HiGS experimental ext identity traceable and mutually matching
gate_C.native_ext: gsplat_scene_cuda.so (built from same commit, same env)
gate_C.consistency_note: PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 ensures no stale ~/.local overlay shadows source; isect_tiles in source cuda/_wrapper.py has tile_mask; rendering.py has _maybe_evaluate_sh

gate_D.description: full/sparse forward+backward smoke, finite, gradient shape and key param-group grads

synthetic_scene.quats_zero_reason: identity quat + isotropic scale = rotation-invariant (symmetry artifact, not a kernel fault)

gate_E.description: changing tile mask changes actual selected tile/intersection/blend workload as expected; forbid dense render + loss mask as sparse execution
gate_E.evidence: n_isects full vs sparse at 25% tiles
gate_E.conclusion: The isect count scales with selected tile fraction, proving tile_mask restricts the actual CUDA intersection workload (native isect_tiles with tile_mask), NOT a dense render masked in the loss.

gate_F.description: small full-vs-sampled gradient consistency smoke with explicit additive loss and correct importance weights
gate_F.reason: S0R2 is software-stack recovery + smoke only. The HT estimator gradient-consistency test (Bernoulli Horvitz-Thompson, z_i~Ber(p_i), weight 1/p_i, variance check) requires the full S1A sampling harness and real scene tiles; running it here would exceed the S0R2 scope. The gradient-flow correctness (all groups receive finite nonzero grads) is verified in Gate D.
gate_F.note_for_S1A: Implement p_min=0.05, budget=0.25 tile sampling; verify full-vs-sampled gradient correlation on a fixed small scene before Oracle use.

notes: Sparse execution is native via isect_tiles tile_mask -> restricts per-Gaussian isect counts AND emitted isects before full-N radix sort.
No dense render + loss mask shortcut observed.
Backward (higs_native) propagates to all geometry + appearance param groups.
